label: Mark 9:1
text:
He said to them,
“Most certainly I tell you, there are some standing here who will in no way taste death until they see God’s Kingdom come with power.”

label: Mark 9:2
text: After six days Jesus took with him Peter, James, and John, and brought them up onto a high mountain privately by themselves, and he was changed into another form in front of them.

label: Mark 9:3
text: His clothing became glistening, exceedingly white, like snow, such as no launderer on earth can whiten them.

label: Mark 9:4
text: Elijah and Moses appeared to them, and they were talking with Jesus.

label: Mark 9:5
text: Peter answered Jesus, “Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. Let’s make three tents: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”

label: Mark 9:7
text: A cloud came, overshadowing them, and a voice came out of the cloud, “This is my beloved Son. Listen to him.”

label: Mark 9:9
text: As they were coming down from the mountain, he commanded them that they should tell no one what things they had seen, until after the Son of Man had risen from the dead.

label: Mark 9:11
text: They asked him, saying, “Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”

label: Mark 9:12
text:
He said to them,
“Elijah indeed comes first, and restores all things. How is it written about the Son of Man, that he should suffer many things and be despised?

label: Mark 9:13
text: But I tell you that Elijah has come, and they have also done to him whatever they wanted to, even as it is written about him.”

label: Mark 9:17
text: One of the multitude answered, “Teacher, I brought to you my son, who has a mute spirit;

label: Mark 9:20
text: They brought him to him, and when he saw him, immediately the spirit convulsed him, and he fell on the ground, wallowing and foaming at the mouth.

label: Mark 9:21
text:
He asked his father,
“How long has it been since this has come to him?”
He said, “From childhood.

label: Mark 9:22
text: Often it has cast him both into the fire and into the water, to destroy him. But if you can do anything, have compassion on us, and help us.”

label: Mark 9:25
text:
When Jesus saw that a multitude came running together, he rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to him,
“You mute and deaf spirit, I command you, come out of him, and never enter him again!”

label: Mark 9:29
text:
He said to them,
“This kind can come out by nothing, except by prayer and fasting.”

label: Mark 9:31
text:
For he was teaching his disciples, and said to them,
“The Son of Man is being handed over to the hands of men, and they will kill him; and when he is killed, on the third day he will rise again.”

label: Mark 9:33
text:
He came to Capernaum, and when he was in the house he asked them,
“What were you arguing among yourselves on the way?”

label: Mark 9:34
text: But they were silent, for they had disputed one with another on the way about who was the greatest.

label: Mark 9:35
text:
He sat down, and called the twelve; and he said to them,
“If any man wants to be first, he shall be last of all, and servant of all.”

label: Mark 9:36
text: He took a little child, and set him in the middle of them. Taking him in his arms, he said to them,

label: Mark 9:37
text: “Whoever receives one such little child in my name, receives me, and whoever receives me, doesn’t receive me, but him who sent me.”

label: Mark 9:38
text: John said to him, “Teacher, we saw someone who doesn’t follow us casting out demons in your name; and we forbade him, because he doesn’t follow us.”

label: Mark 9:41
text: For whoever will give you a cup of water to drink in my name, because you are Christ’s, most certainly I tell you, he will in no way lose his reward.

label: Mark 9:42
text: Whoever will cause one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him if he were thrown into the sea with a millstone hung around his neck.

label: Mark 9:43
text:
If your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter into life maimed, rather than having your two hands to go into Gehenna,

into the unquenchable fire,

label: Mark 9:44
text: ‘where their worm doesn’t die, and the fire is not quenched.’

variants.reading: the verse is absent (the refrain 'where their worm doesn't die, and the fire is not quenched' is not printed)
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'List of omitted Bible verses' records Mark 9:44 and 9:46 as 'both lacking in Codex Sinaiticus, Codex Vaticanus, Codex Ephraemi Rescriptus, Codex Regius, Codex Washingtonianus, Family 1, and some manuscripts of the ancient versions'; they duplicate 9:48, which remains. The UBS text assigns the omission a confidence rating of A. WEB prints the verses; no preserves edge from Sinaiticus or Vaticanus is added for them.

label: Mark 9:45
text:
If your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter into life lame, rather than having your two feet to be cast into Gehenna,

into the fire that will never be quenched—

label: Mark 9:46
text: ‘where their worm doesn’t die, and the fire is not quenched.’

variants.reading: the verse is absent (the refrain 'where their worm doesn't die, and the fire is not quenched' is not printed)
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'List of omitted Bible verses' records Mark 9:44 and 9:46 as 'both lacking in Codex Sinaiticus, Codex Vaticanus, Codex Ephraemi Rescriptus, Codex Regius, Codex Washingtonianus, Family 1, and some manuscripts of the ancient versions'; they duplicate 9:48, which remains. The UBS text assigns the omission a confidence rating of A. WEB prints the verses; no preserves edge from Sinaiticus or Vaticanus is added for them.

label: Mark 9:47
text:
If your eye causes you to stumble, cast it out. It is better for you to enter into God’s Kingdom with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into the Gehenna
of fire,

label: Mark 9:48
text: ‘where their worm doesn’t die, and the fire is not quenched.’

label: Mark 9:49
text: For everyone will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be seasoned with salt.

variants.reading: πας γαρ πυρι αλισθησεται ('everyone will be salted with fire'), without the sacrifice clause
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Mark' (its Mark 9 section lists only 9:49) gives πας γαρ πυρι αλισθησεται for (א εν πυρι) B L W Δ f1 f13 28 565 700 ℓ260 syrs sa - Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and Washingtonianus are manuscript nodes of this graph. WEB prints the fuller reading 'everyone will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be seasoned with salt' (the A K Π reading).

variants.reading: πασα γαρ θυσια αλι αλισθησεται ('every sacrifice shall be salted with salt'), without the fire clause
variants.note: The article lists πασα γαρ θυσια αλι αλισθησεται for D (Codex Bezae) and the Old Latin - neither is a manuscript node of this graph, so attested_by is left empty.

label: Mark 9:50
text: Salt is good, but if the salt has lost its saltiness, with what will you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”

label: His clothing became glistening white, beyond any launderer's work
statement: At the transfiguration Jesus's clothing became glistening, exceedingly white, like snow - 'such as no launderer on earth can whiten them'.

label: A cloud overshadows them and a voice from the cloud speaks
statement: A cloud came overshadowing them, and a voice out of the cloud said, 'This is my beloved Son. Listen to him.'

label: Tell no one what they had seen until the Son of Man had risen
statement: Coming down from the mountain, Jesus commanded Peter, James and John to tell no one what things they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead.
note: Modern scholarship calls this motif the 'messianic secret' (Wrede); that is a modern theory and stays in notes.md, not in the graph as evidence.

label: The boy with the mute and deaf spirit
statement: A father brought his son, possessed from childhood by a mute and deaf spirit that convulsed him, made him foam at the mouth and grind his teeth, and often threw him into fire and water; Jesus rebuked the spirit and it came out.
note: Mark describes the spirit as mute and deaf and gives the symptoms and their duration from childhood; Matthew 17:15 calls the boy 'moonstruck' (seleniazetai). A difference between Gospels, recorded with related_to.

label: This kind comes out only by prayer (and fasting)
statement: 'This kind can come out by nothing, except by prayer and fasting' - deliverance from this kind of spirit was linked to prayer and fasting.
note: The parallel Matthew 17:21 is 'believed to have been assimilated from Mark' (fetched Wikipedia 'List of omitted Bible verses') and is omitted in Matthew by the original hand of Sinaiticus and by Vaticanus; WEB prints it in both Gospels.

label: First of all = last of all and servant of all
statement: 'If any man wants to be first, he shall be last of all, and servant of all.'

label: The stranger casting out demons in Jesus's name
statement: John reported that the disciples had forbidden a man who did not follow them from casting out demons in Jesus's name; Jesus said not to forbid him, for no one doing a mighty work in his name could quickly speak evil of him.

label: The Isaiah 66:24 refrain on Gehenna
statement: Mark quotes Isaiah 66:24 three times as a refrain on Gehenna: 'where their worm doesn't die, and the fire is not quenched.'

label: Everyone salted with fire; every sacrifice seasoned with salt
statement: 'Everyone will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be seasoned with salt' - salt belonged to the sacrificial ritual the saying draws on.

label: Mark 9:6
text: For he didn’t know what to say, for they were very afraid.

label: Mark 9:8
text: Suddenly looking around, they saw no one with them any more, except Jesus only.

label: Mark 9:10
text: They kept this saying to themselves, questioning what the “rising from the dead” meant.

label: Mark 9:14
text: Coming to the disciples, he saw a great multitude around them, and scribes questioning them.

label: Mark 9:15
text: Immediately all the multitude, when they saw him, were greatly amazed, and running to him, greeted him.

label: Mark 9:16
text: He asked the scribes, “What are you asking them?”

label: Mark 9:18
text: and wherever it seizes him, it throws him down, and he foams at the mouth, and grinds his teeth, and wastes away. I asked your disciples to cast it out, and they weren’t able.”

label: Mark 9:19
text: He answered him, “Unbelieving generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I bear with you? Bring him to me.”

label: Mark 9:23
text: Jesus said to him, “If you can believe, all things are possible to him who believes.”

label: Mark 9:24
text: Immediately the father of the child cried out with tears, “I believe. Help my unbelief!”

label: Mark 9:26
text: After crying out and convulsing him greatly, it came out of him. The boy became like one dead; so much that most of them said, “He is dead.”

label: Mark 9:27
text: But Jesus took him by the hand, and raised him up; and he arose.

label: Mark 9:28
text: When he had come into the house, his disciples asked him privately, “Why couldn’t we cast it out?”

label: Mark 9:30
text: They went out from there, and passed through Galilee. He didn’t want anyone to know it.

label: Mark 9:32
text: But they didn’t understand the saying, and were afraid to ask him.

label: Mark 9:39
text: But Jesus said, “Don’t forbid him, for there is no one who will do a mighty work in my name, and be able quickly to speak evil of me.

label: Mark 9:40
text: For whoever is not against us is on our side.
